findings.issue_text: P1: formSchema passed to zodResolver was not updated to include backupCode, so zod object stripping may omit backupCode from submit values, causing signIn credentials to lack backupCode, triggering the TOTP branch and a silent login loop; e2e coverage for backup-code login is left as a TODO

P2: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (read array, indexOf, write back with null), allowing two concurrent logins with the same valid code to both succeed, violating the single-use guarantee; needs a transaction or atomic compare-and-swap

P2: Backup code comparison is case/format-sensitive: codes are lowercase hex but indexOf comparison after only dash-stripping rejects uppercase input; input field lacks autoCapitalize='none'/autoCorrect='off' and surrounding whitespace in pasted codes fails, giving false 'incorrect code' errors in a recovery flow

P3: disable.ts uses req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '') without validation, so non-string body values (e.g. number or object) throw an unhandled TypeError returning 500 instead of a 400 validation error; JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is similarly unguarded, yielding 500 on corrupt stored data instead of a structured ErrorCode

P3: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature have backupCodes === null; the 'Lost access' flow leads to 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' but locked-out users cannot log in to reach settings, making the message a dead-end

P3: EnableTwoFactorModal shows the 'backup codes copied' success toast unconditionally after navigator.clipboard.writeText, which can reject on permission denial or non-secure contexts, so the user is told copying succeeded when it failed and the rejection is unhandled; toast should fire only on resolution with an error path

Backup code field is registered in login form but formSchema and submit handler were not updated, so zod strips the backupCode key and it never reaches the backend, causing backup-code login to silently fall through to the TOTP branch and fail with SecondFactorRequired

Backup code consumption in authorize (next-auth-options.ts:131-155) is a non-atomic check-then-write (indexOf then separate prisma update) with no transaction or compare-and-swap, allowing two concurrent sign-ins to replay the same single-use backup code
Disable endpoint calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") without type checking, so non-string values (e.g. 123 or {}) throw TypeError and cause an unhandled 500

JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) has no try/catch or array validation, so a corrupted blob, rotated encryption key, or non-array JSON value bricks both the disable endpoint and every login attempt for that user until the row is manually fixed

Backup code entropy is only 40 bits per code (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")), and without confirmed per-code-attempt rate limiting on the login and disable paths, an attacker with the password can mount an online guessing attack to bypass or remove 2FA

Backup code single-use enforcement is not atomic (TOCTOU race): check-and-consume in next-auth-options.ts is a non-transactional read-modify-write, so two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass indexOf and replay the code; fix with a transactional updateMany with a where guard, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or optimistic concurrency

Object URL leak in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: backupCodesUrl is only revoked when a new setup response arrives, not on unmount/reopen, leaking a blob URL for the page lifetime; a useEffect cleanup would fix it

Login form zod schema likely not updated for backupCode field — zodResolver strips unknown keys, so credentials.backupCode is undefined in authorize and backup-code login is silently broken (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx ~line 42)

disable.ts user query likely missing backupCodes in Prisma select — user.backupCodes will be undefined and disable-with-backup-code always fails with ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts)

onEnable() no longer fires on successful enable unless user clicks the Close button — parent state diverges if dialog dismissed via ESC or overlay click (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx ~lines 132-136)

resetState() only clears password, errorMessage, and step — backupCodes, secret, dataUri, and Blob URL survive modal close/reopen, keeping secrets resident in memory/DOM (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx ~line 75)

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write — concurrent logins can reuse the same code, breaking the 'exactly once' single-use guarantee (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts ~lines 148-157)

req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") without validating the value is a string — non-string JSON body throws TypeError and surfaces as unhandled 500 HTML instead of a JSON error response (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts ~lines 48-51)

Missing encryption key throws new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) producing a raw 500 HTML response instead of the endpoint's established res.status(...).json({ error }) pattern (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts ~line 68)

Race condition (TOCTOU) in backup-code consumption: non-atomic read-decrypt-compare-then-write in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts (~136-153) allows concurrent logins to consume the same backup code twice or clobber null markers; should be a transactional read-modify-write

Backup code is consumed via prisma.user.update before session issuance completes; if anything later in authorize() throws, the user gets an error but the backup code is permanently burned (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts ~146-154)

backupCode may never reach authorize(): the zod formSchema and signIn('credentials') call in apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx (~85-160) were not updated, so zodResolver may strip backupCode, making the backup-code login path dead

Unhandled exceptions from JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt on stored backup codes in totp/disable.ts (~55) and next-auth-options.ts (~136) — corrupted stored blob causes unhandled 500s or recurring InternalServerError with no recovery path and no MissingBackupCodes fallback error code

Clipboard write in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~272-276) is a promise with no await/.catch, so failures (insecure context, permission denied) cause unhandled rejections while a success toast is shown unconditionally — false 'copied!' confirmation can lead to permanent lockout

Backup codes are persisted server-side during setup (totp/setup.ts ~60-64) before ever being displayed to the user in the DisplayBackupCodes step; aborting between steps leaves unrevealed codes in the DB, an avoidable consistency gap

Blob URL for backup codes in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~92-97) is never revoked on unmount or dialog close (only revoked on a subsequent setup call), leaking object URLs and keeping plaintext backup codes alive in a downloadable blob

Stale lost-access state in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~38, ~105-112): twoFactorLostAccess, errorMessage, and form values are not reset on cancel/dismiss, so reopening the modal lands the user in backup-code mode with a stale error message

When all backup codes are consumed (array is [null, null, ...]), indexOf returns -1 and the user gets IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes, directing a locked-out user to retry codes that can never work (totp/disable.ts ~58-62, next-auth-options.ts ~142)

P1: Core backup-code login logic in next-auth-options.ts:131-156 (single-use consumption, rejection of incorrect codes, MissingBackupCodes path, and re-encryption round-trip on partially-consumed lists) has zero unit or integration test coverage

P1: Disable-via-backup-code endpoint path in two-factor/totp/disable.ts:46-64 is untested, including the JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) behavior on corrupted data and the non-obvious invariant that codes are wiped on disable rather than consumed
P1: New e2e test only verifies backup code display; the actual feature of using a backup code to log in, verifying single-use rejection, or disabling 2FA via backup code is never exercised end-to-end

P2: E2E assertions verify side-effect signals instead of actual output — download only checks suggestedFilename() (file content unverified) and copy only checks that the toast appears, which fires unconditionally even if clipboard write fails or writes the wrong string

P2: No tests for the new lost-access UI flows in login.tsx:104-133 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38-78, including toggle state machine, form field clearing, error message mapping, and the behavior change from multiple if-blocks to an else-if chain in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:66-76

P3: Pre-existing broken assertion in login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-52 (isChecked() truthiness trap) is flagged with a FIXME but not fixed, so the '2FA enabled' setup step is not actually verified before new backup-code assertions run
Zod schema for login form not updated for backupCode, so handleSubmit strips backupCode before signIn, causing backup-code login to fall through to TOTP branch and always return SecondFactorRequired

Backup-code verification logic (decrypt, JSON.parse, indexOf check) duplicated across totp/disable.ts and next-auth-options.ts with diverging behavior (consume vs delete), creating maintenance risk with no shared helper or type

EnableTwoFactorModal dialog can be dismissed via Esc/overlay/onOpenChange at backup-codes step without calling onEnable or resetState, leaving server-side 2FA enabled but parent uninformed and stale state persisting for reopening

Unguarded JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) on login path throws on corrupt/truncated ciphertext or rotated encryption key, causing unhandled 500 in disable.ts and raw parsing error in authorize instead of a meaningful ErrorCode
Backup-code matching is case-sensitive via exact indexOf while UI placeholder suggests uppercase, so users transcribing codes as uppercase always get IncorrectBackupCode
BackupCode.tsx default export is internally named TwoFactor, a copy-paste remnant confusing grep/refactoring

backupCodesUrl object URL never revoked on unmount or dialog close (leaking object URL containing secrets), and resetState leaves backupCodes, dataUri, and secret in component state after modal closes
Known-broken vacuous test assertion (two-factor-switch passes even when unchecked) and zero test coverage for backup-code login and disable-with-backup-code flows committed with TODO/FIXME

P1: Same backup code can be consumed twice due to non-atomic read-modify-write in next-auth-options.ts (~140-156): fetch → decrypt → indexOf → mutate → update allows concurrent logins to both succeed with one code (lost update); needs an atomic compare-and-swap update or transaction with row lock

P1: Existing 2FA users can never obtain backup codes: they have backupCodes = null (no backfill), but backup codes are only generated during the setup flow reachable via the Enable modal when 2FA is disabled, so existing users must disable and re-enroll 2FA to get codes; the missing_backup_codes error message points to a flow that doesn't exist for them

P1: backupCode may be stripped by the zod resolver in login.tsx (~67, ~218): formSchema likely doesn't include the new backupCode field and zod strips unknown keys by default, so the sign-in callback receives a payload without backupCode, making backup-code login fail and return SecondFactorRequired with a misleading error

P2: Dialog dismissal on the backup-codes step skips onEnable() and cleanup in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~200-290): ESC/outside-click close via onOpenChange doesn't notify the parent (2FA enabled server-side but parent UI unaware) and doesn't call resetState(), leaving backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, secret, and dataUri in component state (stale plaintext codes may linger in memory)

P3: Non-string backupCode causes an unhandled 500: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") throws TypeError for non-string JSON body values in disable.ts (~58) and next-auth-options.ts (~150); should be type-checked before use

Copy button shows 'backup_codes_copied' success toast without awaiting or catching navigator.clipboard.writeText, so the success toast fires even when the clipboard write fails (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~270-276)

E2E suite has an acknowledged false-green assertion: the test gating 2FA enabled passes even when the switch is unchecked (FIXME in diff), and backup-code assertions only check filename/toast presence rather than content (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-52 and :110-125)

Unguarded JSON.parse on decrypted backupCodes with no try/catch in both the disable endpoint and authorize path; corrupted data, partial write, or key mismatch throws an unstructured 500 or generic auth error instead of proper messaging (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:~53 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:~141)

Disable modal 'lost access' state and errorMessage persist across cancel/reopen, landing the user in backup-code mode with a stale error and silently changing which credential the next submit sends; enable modal resets state but disable modal does not (apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~37, ~110)

Backup codes are lowercase hex compared case-sensitively, but the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder invites uppercase entry, so manually transcribed uppercase codes fail with IncorrectBackupCode and no case hint; no toLowerCase() normalization anywhere (apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:20-23 / disable.ts:~57 / next-auth-options.ts:~145)

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })` and adds a `backupCode` field/UI, but it does not include the definition of `formSchema`, so the claim that the zod schema was not updated (and is stripping `backupCode` from submit values) cannot be verified from this PR diff alone. The only directly verifiable part is a TODO comment about adding more backup-code tests, which by itself doesn’t substantiate the asserted login-loop defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (read array, indexOf, write back with null), allowing two concurrent logins with the same valid code to both succeed, violating the single-use guarantee; needs a transaction or atomic compare-and-swap

P2: Backup code comparison is case/format-sensitive: codes are lowercase hex but indexOf comparison after only dash-stripping rejects uppercase input; input field lacks autoCapitalize='none'/autoCorrect='off' and surrounding whitespace in pasted codes fails, giving false 'incorrect code' errors in a recovery flow

P3: disable.ts uses req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-', '') without validation, so non-string body values (e.g. number or object) throw an unhandled TypeError returning 500 instead of a 400 validation error; JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is similarly unguarded, yielding 500 on corrupt stored data instead of a structured ErrorCode

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the backup-code path does `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` guarded only by a truthy check (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`). If `backupCode` is a non-string truthy value (e.g. object/number), `replaceAll` will throw a `TypeError`, which is not handled here and would result in a 500 rather than a structured 400 error. Similarly, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` is unguarded; corrupt/invalid decrypted data would throw and also likely produce a 500. Both are correctness/robustness defects in the new logic introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature have backupCodes === null; the 'Lost access' flow leads to 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' but locked-out users cannot log in to reach settings, making the message a dead-end

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds optional `User.backupCodes` (nullable) and only populates it during new 2FA setup (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` stores encrypted `backupCodes`). For users who already had `twoFactorEnabled` before this change, `backupCodes` will remain null (no backfill). In the new “Lost access” login path (`pages/auth/login.tsx` toggles `twoFactorLostAccess` to show `<BackupCode/>`), NextAuth authorize explicitly throws `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` but `!user.backupCodes` (`next-auth-options.ts`). The UI maps that to `t("missing_backup_codes")` (“Please generate them in your settings”), which is not actionable for someone who can’t pass TOTP to log in. This is a real dead-end for the intended recovery flow for existing 2FA users without backup codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: EnableTwoFactorModal shows the 'backup codes copied' success toast unconditionally after navigator.clipboard.writeText, which can reject on permission denial or non-secure contexts, so the user is told copying succeeded when it failed and the rejection is unhandled; toast should fire only on resolution with an error path

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal’s backup codes step, the Copy button handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` without awaiting or handling rejection (`catch`). Since `writeText` returns a Promise and can fail (e.g., permission denied, insecure context), this will display a success toast even when copying fails and will also leave an unhandled promise rejection. This behavior is directly visible in the diff in the `data-testid="backup-codes-copy"` onClick implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code field is registered in login form but formSchema and submit handler were not updated, so zod strips the backupCode key and it never reaches the backend, causing backup-code login to silently fall through to the TOTP branch and fail with SecondFactorRequired

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` the UI now conditionally renders `<BackupCode />`, which registers `backupCode` via `react-hook-form` (`methods.register("backupCode")`), and the `LoginValues` interface was extended with `backupCode`. However, the diff does not show any corresponding update to the Zod `formSchema` used by `useForm({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })`, nor any change to the login submit/signIn payload to include `backupCode`. With Zod’s default behavior (strip unknown keys), an unmodeled `backupCode` would be dropped and never reach the backend, making “lost access” backup-code login fail (backend would still treat it as missing second factor).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code consumption in authorize (next-auth-options.ts:131-155) is a non-atomic check-then-write (indexOf then separate prisma update) with no transaction or compare-and-swap, allowing two concurrent sign-ins to replay the same single-use backup code

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code path decrypts `user.backupCodes`, does `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, and then performs a separate `prisma.user.update` after setting `backupCodes[index] = null`. This is a classic check-then-write without a transaction/conditional update, so two concurrent sign-ins using the same valid backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update commits, allowing replay of what is meant to be a single-use code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disable endpoint calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") without type checking, so non-string values (e.g. 123 or {}) throw TypeError and cause an unhandled 500

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path does `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` guarded only by `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`. That condition allows any truthy non-string (e.g., number/object) to pass, and calling `.replaceAll` on a non-string will throw a `TypeError`. The diff shows no local type check/cast before calling `replaceAll`, and no shown error handling around that block, so this can surface as an unhandled 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) has no try/catch or array validation, so a corrupted blob, rotated encryption key, or non-array JSON value bricks both the disable endpoint and every login attempt for that user until the row is manually fixed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds unguarded `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` in both the disable endpoint (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`) and NextAuth authorize flow (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`). If `backupCodes` is corrupted, the encryption key changes, or the decrypted value isn’t valid JSON/array, `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` can throw and bubble up as an unhandled error (500), breaking backup-code disable/login flows for that user. (The finding overstates it as breaking *every* login attempt—TOTP login path doesn’t parse backup codes—but the lack of try/catch/validation is a real defect.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code entropy is only 40 bits per code (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")), and without confirmed per-code-attempt rate limiting on the login and disable paths, an attacker with the password can mount an online guessing attack to bypass or remove 2FA

adjudication.rationale: The diff does generate backup codes as `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` (10 hex chars = 5 bytes = ~40 bits) in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, and both login (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` accepts `credentials.backupCode`) and 2FA disable (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` checks `req.body.backupCode`) now allow authentication/disable via those codes. The diff does not show any explicit attempt throttling/lockout in the new disable handler or in the added backup-code branch of `authorize`, so it’s a concrete security-hardening concern (entropy/online-guessing + rate limiting), but whether existing global rate limiting already applies cannot be confirmed from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code single-use enforcement is not atomic (TOCTOU race): check-and-consume in next-auth-options.ts is a non-transactional read-modify-write, so two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass indexOf and replay the code; fix with a transactional updateMany with a where guard, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or optimistic concurrency

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code verification does a non-transactional read/modify/write: it decrypts `user.backupCodes`, checks `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)`, then sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and performs a separate `prisma.user.update(...)`. With concurrent login attempts using the same backup code, both requests can pass the `indexOf` check before either update commits, allowing the same code to be replayed (TOCTOU). This is a real security/correctness defect in the newly added backup-code single-use logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: onEnable() no longer fires on successful enable unless user clicks the Close button — parent state diverges if dialog dismissed via ESC or overlay click (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx ~lines 132-136)

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, the successful enable path no longer calls onEnable() immediately: when /totp/enable returns 200 it does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and returns (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx around the former `onEnable();`). adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, `resetState()` only does `setPassword("")`, `setErrorMessage(null)`, and `setStep(SetupStep.ConfirmPassword)` (added around the new backup-code flow). It does not clear `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `dataUri`, or `secret` state. The cancel/close handlers call `resetState()`, so after closing the modal those values can remain resident in component state (and the Blob URL is not revoked on close/reset, only when creating a new one). This is a real, diff-grounded security/cleanup concern, though it doesn’t necessarily break visible behavior because `step` is reset so the backup-code UI isn’t rendered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write — concurrent logins can reuse the same code, breaking the 'exactly once' single-use guarantee (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts ~lines 148-157)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code use is implemented as: decrypt `user.backupCodes` (read), `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)` (check), then mutate `backupCodes[index] = null` and `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })` (write). This is a non-atomic read-modify-write without a transaction/locking or conditional update on the prior value, so two concurrent authorize calls can both validate the same backup code before either write occurs, allowing single-use codes to be reused and violating the stated “exactly once” property.

adjudication_records.issue_text: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") without validating the value is a string — non-string JSON body throws TypeError and surfaces as unhandled 500 HTML instead of a JSON error response (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts ~lines 48-51)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code path runs when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` is truthy, and then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If a client sends a non-string but truthy JSON value (e.g., object/number/boolean), `.replaceAll` will throw a `TypeError`. The diff shows no type check/normalization before calling `.replaceAll`, so this can produce an unexpected 500 instead of a controlled JSON error response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing encryption key throws new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) producing a raw 500 HTML response instead of the endpoint's established res.status(...).json({ error }) pattern (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts ~line 68)

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch checks `!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and then does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);` instead of returning `res.status(...).json({ error: ... })`. This can bypass the endpoint’s established JSON error handling (used elsewhere in the same handler for other failures) and likely results in a generic Next.js 500 response rather than a structured `{ error }` payload, breaking callers expecting JSON.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Race condition (TOCTOU) in backup-code consumption: non-atomic read-decrypt-compare-then-write in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts (~136-153) allows concurrent logins to consume the same backup code twice or clobber null markers; should be a transactional read-modify-write

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code verification does a non-atomic read/decrypt/compare followed by a separate `prisma.user.update` write (`backupCodes[index] = null` then re-encrypt + update). With concurrent login attempts using the same backup code, both requests can decrypt the same pre-update list, both find the code present, and both succeed before either update is committed, allowing the same one-time backup code to be used more than once and/or causing lost updates when writing the mutated array back.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is consumed via prisma.user.update before session issuance completes; if anything later in authorize() throws, the user gets an error but the backup code is permanently burned (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts ~146-154)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup code is immediately marked as used and persisted via `await prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })` inside the `authorize()` flow (after verifying the code). This happens before `authorize()` completes successfully (i.e., before it returns the user to NextAuth for session/token issuance). If any subsequent step in `authorize()` (or immediately after returning, during NextAuth token/session generation) fails, the user would see an auth error but the backup code has already been burned in the database, causing irreversible loss of that code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCode may never reach authorize(): the zod formSchema and signIn('credentials') call in apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx (~85-160) were not updated, so zodResolver may strip backupCode, making the backup-code login path dead

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` the form now includes `backupCode` in `LoginValues` and renders `<BackupCode />` (which registers `backupCode`), but the diff does not show any update to the `formSchema` used by `zodResolver(formSchema)`. With Zod object schemas defaulting to stripping unknown keys, `backupCode` would be removed from the validated submit data unless the schema was updated/passthrough, which could prevent the credentials `authorize()` backup-code branch (`credentials.backupCode`) from ever being exercised from the web login form. The diff also doesn’t show any explicit inclusion of `backupCode` in the `signIn('credentials', ...)` payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled exceptions from JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt on stored backup codes in totp/disable.ts (~55) and next-auth-options.ts (~136) — corrupted stored blob causes unhandled 500s or recurring InternalServerError with no recovery path and no MissingBackupCodes fallback error code

adjudication.rationale: In both `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the new backup-code flow does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` on `user.backupCodes` without any try/catch. If the encrypted blob is corrupted/invalid JSON (or decrypt fails), this will throw and bubble up as an unhandled exception (500 / InternalServerError), and it will not return the intended structured errors like `MissingBackupCodes`/`IncorrectBackupCode` (only `!user.backupCodes` is handled).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Clipboard write in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~272-276) is a promise with no await/.catch, so failures (insecure context, permission denied) cause unhandled rejections while a success toast is shown unconditionally — false 'copied!' confirmation can lead to permanent lockout

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the backup code copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` but does not `await` it or attach a `.catch`. The success toast (`showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")`) is shown unconditionally right after the call, so a clipboard failure (e.g., permission denied / insecure context) would still display “copied” and may also surface as an unhandled promise rejection. This is directly verifiable in the diff around the `backup-codes-copy` button handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are persisted server-side during setup (totp/setup.ts ~60-64) before ever being displayed to the user in the DisplayBackupCodes step; aborting between steps leaves unrevealed codes in the DB, an avoidable consistency gap

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `totp/setup.ts` now generates `backupCodes` and immediately persists them in `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) , twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }})` before 2FA is actually enabled. In the UI (`EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`), backup codes are only displayed in the later `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, which is reached only after the separate enable call succeeds (`if (response.status === 200) { setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes); }`). If the user cancels/closes after setup (QR/secret fetched) but before enable completes, the DB will contain backup codes the user was never shown. This is a real consistency/UX/security hygiene concern, but not a directly verifiable functional break in the diff since backup-code auth paths also check `twoFactorEnabled` before accepting backup codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blob URL for backup codes in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~92-97) is never revoked on unmount or dialog close (only revoked on a subsequent setup call), leaking object URLs and keeping plaintext backup codes alive in a downloadable blob

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, a Blob URL is created and stored in state (`setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))`) and only revoked when a subsequent setup call happens (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl)`). `resetState()` (called on cancel/close and when finishing via “close”) does not revoke the existing `backupCodesUrl`, and there is no unmount/useEffect cleanup shown. This can leak object URLs and keep the plaintext backup codes blob alive longer than necessary.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale lost-access state in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~38, ~105-112): twoFactorLostAccess, errorMessage, and form values are not reset on cancel/dismiss, so reopening the modal lands the user in backup-code mode with a stale error message

adjudication.rationale: In DisableTwoFactorModal, the new state `twoFactorLostAccess` and `errorMessage` (plus form fields via react-hook-form) are only reset on success (`setTwoFactorLostAccess(false); resetForm();`) or when toggling the lost-access button (`resetForm(false)`). The Cancel button still calls only `onCancel` with no local reset, and there is no `useEffect` tied to `open`/dismissal to clear state. If the modal is hidden without unmounting (common for dialogs), reopening would indeed preserve `twoFactorLostAccess` and any previous error/form values, landing the user back in backup-code mode with stale UI state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When all backup codes are consumed (array is [null, null, ...]), indexOf returns -1 and the user gets IncorrectBackupCode instead of MissingBackupCodes, directing a locked-out user to retry codes that can never work (totp/disable.ts ~58-62, next-auth-options.ts ~142)

adjudication.rationale:
Verified in both places cited. In `next-auth-options.ts`, successful backup-code login sets the matched entry to `null` and re-encrypts (`backupCodes[index] = null; ... symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes)...)`). Once all codes are consumed the stored JSON can become `[null, null, ...]` while `user.backupCodes` remains non-null, so the guard `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes` will not trigger. The subsequent lookup `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` returns `-1` on an array of nulls, causing `IncorrectBackupCode` instead of a more accurate `MissingBackupCodes`.

The same pattern exists in `pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`: it only returns `MissingBackupCodes` when `user.backupCodes` is falsy, then does `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` and returns `IncorrectBackupCode` on `-1`, so an all-null list would also surface as incorrect rather than missing/none left.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Core backup-code login logic in next-auth-options.ts:131-156 (single-use consumption, rejection of incorrect codes, MissingBackupCodes path, and re-encryption round-trip on partially-consumed lists) has zero unit or integration test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new backup-code authentication logic in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (new `backupCode` credential field; decrypting `user.backupCodes`; rejecting incorrect codes / `MissingBackupCodes`; and consuming a code by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting via `symmetricEncrypt` + `prisma.user.update`). In the shown diff, there are no unit tests added around `authorize()` for these new branches, and the only related e2e change (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`) includes a TODO/FIXME and tests backup code display/copy/download—not backup-code login or single-use consumption. This is a specific, diff-grounded coverage gap for nontrivial auth logic, not a direct functional defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Disable-via-backup-code endpoint path in two-factor/totp/disable.ts:46-64 is untested, including the JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) behavior on corrupted data and the non-obvious invariant that codes are wiped on disable rather than consumed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new disable flow that accepts `backupCode` (DisableTwoFactorModal -> `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode, backupCode)` and `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` backup-code branch). There are no tests in the diff covering this new server-side branch, and the existing Playwright file explicitly notes missing backup-code tests (`// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`). The branch includes nontrivial behavior that would benefit from coverage: decrypt+`JSON.parse(...)` of `user.backupCodes` with no guarding against corrupted data, and the (non-obvious) behavior that disabling 2FA wipes `backupCodes: null` for the user rather than consuming a single code. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: New e2e test only verifies backup code display; the actual feature of using a backup code to log in, verifying single-use rejection, or disabling 2FA via backup code is never exercised end-to-end

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the newly added coverage after enabling 2FA only interacts with the backup-code UI (download/copy/close via `backup-codes-*` testids) and even includes a comment `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. The diff adds substantial backup-code logic for login (`next-auth-options.ts` handling `credentials.backupCode`) and disabling 2FA via backup code (`pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` branch on `req.body.backupCode`), but no e2e test exercises logging in with a backup code, single-use behavior/rejection, or disabling 2FA using a backup code end-to-end.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: E2E assertions verify side-effect signals instead of actual output — download only checks suggestedFilename() (file content unverified) and copy only checks that the toast appears, which fires unconditionally even if clipboard write fails or writes the wrong string

adjudication.rationale: In the new E2E additions (`apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`), the download test only asserts `download.suggestedFilename()` and explicitly leaves content validation as `// TODO: check file content`. Similarly, the copy test only clicks `backup-codes-copy` and waits for `toast-success`, with `// TODO: check clipboard content`. In the UI code (`EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`), the copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without awaiting/handling failures and then immediately calls `showToast(...)`, so the toast is not a reliable signal that the clipboard contains the expected text. This is a concrete test robustness gap introduced by the diff, not a functional product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No tests for the new lost-access UI flows in login.tsx:104-133 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:38-78, including toggle state machine, form field clearing, error message mapping, and the behavior change from multiple if-blocks to an else-if chain in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:66-76

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new lost-access flows and state transitions in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (new `twoFactorLostAccess` state, footer toggle buttons, and clearing `totpCode`/`backupCode` + `setErrorMessage(null)`), and in `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` (new `twoFactorLostAccess`, `resetForm()`, conditional rendering of `<BackupCode/>` vs `<TwoFactor autoFocus={false}/>` and new error mappings for `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`, plus a changed `if` chain to `else if`). The only added Playwright coverage (`login.2fa.e2e.ts`) tests backup-code display/copy/download during enable, and even contains a `// TODO: add more backup code tests` comment—there are no tests in the diff that exercise the login lost-access toggle/state machine or the disable-modal toggle + form clearing + error mapping behavior. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Pre-existing broken assertion in login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-52 (isChecked() truthiness trap) is flagged with a FIXME but not fixed, so the '2FA enabled' setup step is not actually verified before new backup-code assertions run

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` the diff adds a FIXME noting that `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` “passes even when switch is not checked”. The code still uses that pattern (passing the `Promise<boolean>` from `isChecked()` directly into `expect(...).toBeTruthy()`), rather than asserting `toBeChecked()` or `expect(await ...isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`. So the “2FA enabled” state is not reliably verified before the newly added backup-code UI assertions run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zod schema for login form not updated for backupCode, so handleSubmit strips backupCode before signIn, causing backup-code login to fall through to TOTP branch and always return SecondFactorRequired

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `backupCode` to `LoginValues` and introduces the `BackupCode` field in `login.tsx`, but it does not show the definition of `formSchema` used by `zodResolver(formSchema)`. Since the Zod schema itself is not included/changed in this diff, the claim that it was "not updated" and that `handleSubmit`/resolver strips `backupCode` cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code verification logic (decrypt, JSON.parse, indexOf check) duplicated across totp/disable.ts and next-auth-options.ts with diverging behavior (consume vs delete), creating maintenance risk with no shared helper or type

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows backup-code verification logic duplicated in two places: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (decrypt + `JSON.parse` + `indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`) and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (same pattern for `credentials.backupCode`). The behaviors do diverge: the NextAuth flow consumes a single code by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting, while the disable endpoint does not consume one code and instead later clears all codes via `backupCodes: null` when disabling 2FA. This is a concrete maintenance/consistency risk introduced by the change, though not necessarily a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal dialog can be dismissed via Esc/overlay/onOpenChange at backup-codes step without calling onEnable or resetState, leaving server-side 2FA enabled but parent uninformed and stale state persisting for reopening

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after successful enable (handleEnable), it sets `step` to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()` (line where it used to call onEnable). At that step, the Cancel button is intentionally hidden, and only the explicit “close” button calls `resetState(); onEnable();`. However the Dialog is still controlled via `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` and there is no wrapping logic to call `resetState`/`onEnable` when the user dismisses the dialog via Esc or overlay click. That means the modal can close without notifying the parent via `onEnable()` and without clearing internal `step/backupCodes/...` state, causing stale state when reopened and potentially leaving the parent UI out of sync with server-side 2FA already enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) on login path throws on corrupt/truncated ciphertext or rotated encryption key, causing unhandled 500 in disable.ts and raw parsing error in authorize instead of a meaningful ErrorCode

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new unguarded `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` for `backupCodes` in two login/2FA paths: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (`const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))`) and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` inside `authorize()` (same pattern). Neither location wraps decrypt/parse in a try/catch or converts failures into an `ErrorCode`. If the ciphertext is corrupt/truncated, the encryption key is rotated/mismatched, or the decrypted payload isn’t valid JSON, `symmetricDecrypt` and/or `JSON.parse` can throw, leading to an unhandled 500 in the API route and a raw thrown error in `authorize()` rather than a controlled `ErrorCode` response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code matching is case-sensitive via exact indexOf while UI placeholder suggests uppercase, so users transcribing codes as uppercase always get IncorrectBackupCode

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex strings (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `totp/setup.ts`), stored, and later matched with `indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` (and similarly in `next-auth-options.ts`) without any normalization. If a user types the code with uppercase A-F (UI placeholder `"XXXXX-XXXXX"` suggests uppercase), the string comparison will fail and return `IncorrectBackupCode` even for the correct code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackupCode.tsx default export is internally named TwoFactor, a copy-paste remnant confusing grep/refactoring
matched_golden_ids: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same inconsistency: in BackupCode.tsx the exported/default component/function is named TwoFactor, suggesting a copy-paste/incorrect naming that doesn’t match the backup code purpose/file name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCodesUrl object URL never revoked on unmount or dialog close (leaking object URL containing secrets), and resetState leaves backupCodes, dataUri, and secret in component state after modal closes
matched_golden_ids: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly identifies that the backupCodesUrl object URL is never revoked on unmount (and also on dialog close), which is the same underlying issue as the golden comment about not revoking the object URL leading to a memory leak. Extra notes about secrets in state do not conflict with the match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Known-broken vacuous test assertion (two-factor-switch passes even when unchecked) and zero test coverage for backup-code login and disable-with-backup-code flows committed with TODO/FIXME

adjudication.rationale: The diff itself flags (and implements) a vacuous Playwright assertion: `await expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` passes a Promise<boolean> to `expect` without awaiting `isChecked()`, which will be truthy regardless of the switch state (matching the added `FIXME` comment). This is a real, verifiable defect in the test introduced/retained in the diff; the additional TODO about missing backup-code flow tests is also present but the broken assertion alone qualifies as a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Same backup code can be consumed twice due to non-atomic read-modify-write in next-auth-options.ts (~140-156): fetch → decrypt → indexOf → mutate → update allows concurrent logins to both succeed with one code (lost update); needs an atomic compare-and-swap update or transaction with row lock
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same race condition: backup codes are read/decrypted, checked, mutated, and written back in a non-atomic way, allowing two concurrent logins using the same code to both pass and consume it (lost update), violating one-time-use semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Existing 2FA users can never obtain backup codes: they have backupCodes = null (no backfill), but backup codes are only generated during the setup flow reachable via the Enable modal when 2FA is disabled, so existing users must disable and re-enroll 2FA to get codes; the missing_backup_codes error message points to a flow that doesn't exist for them

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a nullable `backupCodes` column (migration + schema) but only populates it during the TOTP setup endpoint (`/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` generates and stores encrypted `backupCodes`). There is no diff-shown backfill or separate “generate backup codes” flow for users who already have `twoFactorEnabled = true` with `backupCodes = null`. Those users can still use TOTP to disable and re-enroll to get codes (so it’s not “never”), but the new `MissingBackupCodes` path (e.g., login/disable endpoints) can be hit and the message points generally to “generate them in your settings” without any explicit regeneration path in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: backupCode may be stripped by the zod resolver in login.tsx (~67, ~218): formSchema likely doesn't include the new backupCode field and zod strips unknown keys by default, so the sign-in callback receives a payload without backupCode, making backup-code login fail and return SecondFactorRequired with a misleading error

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `login.tsx` adding `backupCode` to `LoginValues` and wiring `BackupCode` UI, and it uses `zodResolver(formSchema)`, but the diff does not show the definition of `formSchema` or whether it was updated to include `backupCode`. Since the claim hinges on `formSchema` omitting `backupCode` (and Zod stripping it), this is not verifiable from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Dialog dismissal on the backup-codes step skips onEnable() and cleanup in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~200-290): ESC/outside-click close via onOpenChange doesn't notify the parent (2FA enabled server-side but parent UI unaware) and doesn't call resetState(), leaving backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, secret, and dataUri in component state (stale plaintext codes may linger in memory)

adjudication.rationale:
In EnableTwoFactorModal, after a successful enable (handleEnable: response.status===200) the code sets `step` to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` instead of calling `onEnable()`. On that backup-codes step, the Cancel button is not rendered (`{step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? ... : null}`), and the only path that calls `onEnable()` is the explicit “close” button. The Dialog is controlled by `open`/`onOpenChange` props (`<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>`), but there is no wrapper around `onOpenChange` to ensure that ESC/outside-click close triggers `onEnable()` or at least local cleanup. Therefore, dismissing the dialog via ESC/outside-click can close it without notifying the parent that 2FA was enabled server-side.

Additionally, the local `resetState()` only clears `password`, `errorMessage`, and `step`; it does not clear `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`, `secret`, or `dataUri`, so even when resetState is invoked (e.g., cancel/close), those values can linger in component state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Non-string backupCode causes an unhandled 500: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") throws TypeError for non-string JSON body values in disable.ts (~58) and next-auth-options.ts (~150); should be type-checked before use

adjudication.rationale: In both API paths the diff calls `.replaceAll("-", "")` on an unvalidated value: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. The only guard is truthiness (`&& req.body.backupCode` / `&& credentials.backupCode`), so a non-string truthy JSON value (e.g., number/object) would reach `.replaceAll` and throw a `TypeError`, resulting in an unhandled 500. This is a real robustness/correctness bug introduced by the new backup-code logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Download button inside the enable <Form> may re-trigger submit in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~276-282): unlike the copy/close buttons, the download button doesn't call e.preventDefault(), so if Button defaults to type="submit", clicking it re-fires handleEnable with the consumed TOTP code, producing a spurious error/toast

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, the backup-codes UI is rendered inside `<Form handleSubmit={handleEnable} ...>`. The `close` and `copy` buttons explicitly call `e.preventDefault()` in their `onClick`, but the `download` control is an `<a>` wrapping a `<Button ...>` with no `type` and no `preventDefault`. In HTML, a button inside a form defaults to `type="submit"`, so clicking “download” can re-trigger the form submit (`handleEnable`) after the TOTP code was already consumed, causing a spurious error/toast. The diff shows this inconsistency and the potential re-submit path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (verify-then-write race): concurrent logins with the same valid code both succeed, and concurrent logins with two different codes can resurrect a spent code via last-write-wins in packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:~131-156

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup code use does a non-atomic read/verify then write: it decrypts `user.backupCodes`, finds `index`, then sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and persists the entire array via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...) } })`. With concurrent requests, both can read the same pre-update value and pass verification. Two logins using the same code can both succeed (both writes set the same index to null), and two logins using different codes can “resurrect” the other spent code because the last write overwrites the full array based on stale state (last-write-wins).

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCode field is added to LoginValues and registered in the form, but formSchema used by zodResolver was not updated, so Zod strips the unknown key and backupCode never reaches the signIn payload, causing a silent-pass login failure with no error shown (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:~67)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `backupCode` to `LoginValues` and introduces a `BackupCode` component that registers `methods.register("backupCode")`, and the login page uses `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })`. However, there is no corresponding diff updating `formSchema` to include `backupCode`. With Zod object schemas defaulting to stripping unknown keys, the validated submit payload produced by `zodResolver` would omit `backupCode`, preventing it from reaching the NextAuth credentials (`credentials.backupCode` was added in `next-auth-options.ts`) and breaking backup-code login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes display dialog can be dismissed via Escape or outside click without confirmation or resetState(), permanently losing the user's only copy of the recovery codes with no way to re-display them (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~165-172, ~200-206)

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal the backup codes are only shown in the new SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes step, and the explicit close path (the “close” button) calls resetState() + onEnable(). However the <Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}> does not wrap onOpenChange to call resetState(), and the “cancel” button is hidden when step === DisplayBackupCodes. If the Dialog component permits closing via Escape/outside click, that would dismiss the backup-code display without running resetState()/any confirmation, meaning the user could lose the only in-UI chance to copy/download the codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Copy button shows 'backup_codes_copied' success toast without awaiting or catching navigator.clipboard.writeText, so the success toast fires even when the clipboard write fails (apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~270-276)

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, the “copy” button handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` without `await`/`.then` or `.catch`. Since `writeText` can reject (e.g., permissions, insecure context), the success toast can display even when the copy fails, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2E suite has an acknowledged false-green assertion: the test gating 2FA enabled passes even when the switch is unchecked (FIXME in diff), and backup-code assertions only check filename/toast presence rather than content (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts:50-52 and :110-125)

adjudication.rationale: The diff itself flags a flaky/false-green E2E assertion: in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` there’s a `// FIXME: this passes even when switch is not checked` comment next to `expect(...isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`, indicating the current gate can incorrectly pass. Additionally, the new backup-code checks only assert download filename and toast presence, with explicit `// TODO: check file content` and `// TODO: check clipboard content`, so they don’t validate the actual backup codes behavior/content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded JSON.parse on decrypted backupCodes with no try/catch in both the disable endpoint and authorize path; corrupted data, partial write, or key mismatch throws an unstructured 500 or generic auth error instead of proper messaging (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:~53 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:~141)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code flows that do `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` without guarding against exceptions in both the disable API route (`apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, where `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`) and the NextAuth authorize path (`packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, same pattern). If decryption fails (e.g., key mismatch) or the stored value is corrupted/not valid JSON, `symmetricDecrypt` and/or `JSON.parse` can throw, leading to an unstructured 500 (API route) or a generic thrown auth error, rather than a controlled error response/message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disable modal 'lost access' state and errorMessage persist across cancel/reopen, landing the user in backup-code mode with a stale error and silently changing which credential the next submit sends; enable modal resets state but disable modal does not (apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:~37, ~110)

adjudication.rationale: In DisableTwoFactorModal, new local state `twoFactorLostAccess` and `errorMessage` are introduced, and form fields are cleared only via `resetForm()` on successful disable or when toggling the "lost_access" button. The Cancel button still calls only `onCancel` (no `resetForm()` / `setTwoFactorLostAccess(false)`), and there is no `useEffect` tied to `open`/`onOpenChange` to reset state on close/reopen. If the modal component remains mounted across closes (typical for dialogs), the user can reopen in backup-code mode with a stale `errorMessage`, and the next submit will send `backupCode` vs `totpCode` based on that persisted state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are lowercase hex compared case-sensitively, but the XXXXX-XXXXX placeholder invites uppercase entry, so manually transcribed uppercase codes fail with IncorrectBackupCode and no case hint; no toLowerCase() normalization anywhere (apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:20-23 / disable.ts:~57 / next-auth-options.ts:~145)
matched_golden_ids: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue describes the same underlying problem: backup codes are validated with a case-sensitive comparison, causing uppercase hex input to fail, and suggests normalizing (e.g., toLowerCase) to make validation case-insensitive.
